rewrites.title: Primed versus naive hysteresis comparison
rewrites.description: Pre-stimulate cells (e.g., with EGF, TPA, or a cytokine), withdraw the stimulus for varied rest periods, then restimulate and compare dose-response and induction-kinetics curves of AP-1 target genes against naive cells. Differences in amplitude, threshold, or speed of the second response, plotted across stimulus history, quantify memory.

rewrites.title: Site-specific disruption of AP-1 motifs at enhancers
rewrites.description: Use dCas9-based tools or base-editing motif mutation to block or remove AP-1 motifs at specific enhancers that gained accessibility after priming. Then test whether transcription of the linked genes upon re-stimulation is selectively reduced, which tests whether specific AP-1-marked loci causally carry the memory for particular downstream genes.

rewrites.title: AP-1 occupancy versus histone mark retention over time
rewrites.description: Run CUT&RUN or ChIP-seq for c-Fos and c-Jun together with histone marks across a stimulation and washout time course. This shows whether memory is carried by histone marks retained after AP-1 has left the chromatin (bookmarking), or whether AP-1 must rebind at each re-exposure.

rewrites.title: Mitotic retention of AP-1 sites and daughter-cell inheritance
rewrites.description: Profile AP-1 binding and chromatin accessibility in synchronized mitotic cells and in freshly divided daughter pairs to see whether AP-1-marked sites are retained through chromosome condensation. Pair this with live imaging of reporter reactivation timing in daughters to test whether physical inheritance, rather than re-establishment from signaling, carries the memory.

rewrites.title: AP-1 transmission through mitosis with cell-cycle-timed degron depletion
rewrites.description: Use live imaging of tagged JUN/FOS through mitosis, mitotic-chromosome CUT&RUN, and lineage tracing of sister cells after a stimulus pulse, with acute degron (dTAG) depletion of AP-1 members at different cell-cycle phases. Transmission of memory to daughter cells only when AP-1 is present during mitosis would show a bookmarking-based memory mechanism.

rewrites.title: Domain-swap test of AP-1 identity versus generic occupancy
rewrites.description: Fuse the AP-1 bZIP DNA-binding domain to non-AP-1 activation domains, and fuse unrelated DNA-binding domains to AP-1 activation domains, matching occupancy at the same enhancers by ChIP and dosing. If memory tracks AP-1 identity and not just occupancy or transactivation strength, systematic swapping should identify the domains that matter for persistence.

rewrites.title: Decay of AP-1 state similarity across sister, cousin, and second-cousin cells
rewrites.description: Use live lineage-tracking microscopy plus endpoint single-cell multiome on microdissected sibling pairs to measure how similarity in AP-1 state between sisters, cousins, and second cousins decays with generational distance after a transient stimulus. Compare the measured decay constant against a null model of random molecular partitioning at mitosis, to distinguish actively maintained, heritable AP-1 states from passive dilution of leftover protein.

rewrites.title: Accelerated decay experiments with extrapolated retention half-life
rewrites.description: Because the memory may outlast a practical experiment, accelerate its loss by raising proliferation rate, forcing and counting divisions by dye dilution, or shifting temperature, and fit the decay rates to extrapolate a retention half-life under normal conditions. This yields a quantitative result, such as the number of divisions over which the AP-1-encoded state persists, rather than a binary answer.

rewrites.title: Ectopic landing-pad test of locus-autonomous memory
rewrites.description: Integrate a primed AP-1 enhancer and a naive copy into the same site-specific landing pad at a neutral genomic locus, then compare retention of the primed state. If memory follows the transplanted enhancer sequence regardless of native chromatin context, the substrate is local DNA/chromatin; if it depends on the native locus, it is a genome-wide or trans-acting state.

rewrites.title: Acute degron removal of AP-1 after the stimulus is withdrawn
rewrites.description: Tag endogenous FOS/JUN family members with an auxin or dTAG degron, let cells establish a primed state, then deplete AP-1 only after the inducing stimulus has been washed out. If accessibility and re-inducibility collapse during depletion and fail to return after the protein is restored, AP-1 is actively maintaining the state rather than having merely initiated it.

rewrites.title: Dimer-resolved AP-1 occupancy after a priming pulse
rewrites.description: Use CUT&Tag or CUT&RUN with knock-in tags for FOS, JUN, and ATF3 at several times after stimulus washout to see whether the sites that stay bound are occupied by a distinct dimer composition, which would identify the memory-bearing complex. This tests whether AP-1 acts as a single uniform complex.

rewrites.title: Bistability and hysteresis from dose-ramp imaging
rewrites.description: Expose cells to ascending and then descending stimulus dose ramps while tracking an AP-1 reporter in each cell, and plot single-cell dose-response curves for each direction. Bimodal distributions and a hysteresis loop (different thresholds on the up and down ramps) would indicate a self-sustaining, positive-feedback memory state rather than a simple graded response.

rewrites.title: Single-cell multiome with lineage tracking across divisions
rewrites.description: Perform single-cell RNA+ATAC on primed versus naive cells over several divisions, using barcodes or sister-cell pairing, to link AP-1 motif accessibility to recall strength. Matched sister-cell behavior would show whether the memory is heritable and AP-1-dependent.

rewrites.title: Acetyl-CoA supply during priming and memory strength
rewrites.description: Manipulate acetyl-CoA availability during the priming window with ACLY inhibition, acetate supplementation, or a citrate-transporter block, then measure H3K27ac at memory enhancers and re-induction kinetics after washout. A dose-dependent effect on memory strength without changes in AP-1 binding would show that metabolic substrate supply, not AP-1 occupancy, sets how much memory is established.

rewrites.title: Allele-specific memory at heterozygous AP-1 motifs
rewrites.description: In F1 hybrid cells, or CRISPR-generated heterozygotes in which the TRE/CRE motif is destroyed on one allele only, use allele-resolved ATAC, CUT&RUN, and nascent RNA to test whether primed accessibility and faster re-induction persist only on the motif-bearing allele within the same nucleus. Because both alleles share the same cytoplasm and trans environment, allele discordance would indicate that the memory is encoded in cis at AP-1 elements rather than inherited as a cellular signaling state.

rewrites.title: Sufficiency test: stimulus-free AP-1 pulse
rewrites.description: Use an optogenetic or chemically dimerizable FOS-JUN, or a dCas9-fused AP-1 activation domain targeted to specific motif sets, to deliver an AP-1 pulse of defined amplitude and duration in otherwise unstimulated cells. Then test whether the later response to a real stimulus is shifted in the same way as in genuinely pre-stimulated cells. Pair this with an acute degron that removes AP-1 only during the quiescent interval to separate establishment from maintenance. This tests whether AP-1 necessity implies AP-1 is the memory mechanism.

rewrites.title: Sister-cell and lineage-tree partitioning of AP-1 state heritability
rewrites.description: Combine live imaging of an AP-1 activity reporter with tracked lineage trees (or expressed lineage barcodes with single-cell multiome) to compute how correlated AP-1 state is between sisters, cousins, and unrelated cells. This partitions AP-1 variation into heritable and transient components and directly estimates how many generations the state survives.

rewrites.title: Time course of AP-1 binding and chromatin opening after stimulus
rewrites.description: After a defined stimulus (e.g., serum, TPA, injury, or inflammatory cue), run time-resolved ATAC-seq, CUT&RUN for FOS/JUN family members, and H3K27ac at many time points during and long after signal withdrawal. Determine which AP-1-bound enhancers stay open or primed, and for how long, to establish whether a persistent record exists and how it decays.

rewrites.title: Acute degron removal after the stimulus ends, at varied delays
rewrites.description: Prime cells, wash out the stimulus, then rapidly degrade AP-1 factors (dTAG or AID) at different delays before restimulation. If the enhanced response and accessibility persist without AP-1, the memory is downstream of it. If they collapse, AP-1 is needed for maintenance and not only for establishment.

rewrites.title: Single-cell multiome with clonal barcodes and live AP-1 reporters
rewrites.description: Use single-cell multiome (ATAC plus RNA) with clonal barcodes, plus live-cell AP-1 activity reporters, to follow whether memory is inherited through cell division in sister cells. Link each cell's past AP-1 activity to its later response. This separates heritable memory from population averaging and shows whether memory is all-or-none or graded.
